title: Founding of Tyre
description: Record first created by the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024)). CFAH dates it as well (added by the CFAH pass); the sort follows the four-tier rule.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH Reply to Beckman (Griffith & White, Part 3): 1251 - 1249 BC. Sort changed by the Reply to Beckman pass (2026-11-13): was provisional 1250 BC.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "A Reply to Beckman’s Defense of Thiele’s Chronology, Part 3: The Founding Dates of Tyre and Carthage," OSF preprint v1.2 (2025), doi:10.17605/OSF.IO/9V65S, Table 2 “Harmonized Chronology of Tyre and Carthage”, row 1251–1249, p. 46
chronologies.note: Tyre founded by survivors of the defeat of Sidon.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 12 "The Rise and Fall of the Amalekite–Phoenician Alliance", PDF p. 284 (printed p. 270)
chronologies.note: A few years after Sidon's defeat in Gideon's time; p. 292 prints "1250 BC".

chronologies.date: “the foundation of the city took place two thousand three hundred years ago”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.44 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 115 (PDF p. 117)
chronologies.note: Priests of Melqart ("Hercules") at Tyre: the temple was as old as the city. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): 450 BC + 2,300 = about 2750 BC. Anchor: CFAH-3 dates Herodotus's visit to Egypt to 450 B.C. (section "Conflicting Information: Herodotus Nine Centuries Below Moeris"; AP-21). CONFLICT: about 400 years before the Flood (2348/2347 BC, CFAH AP-29), and about 1,500 years before Generations' founding of Tyre (about 1250 BC, provisional).
